title: 19 September 2026 · same .41 runtime and model
scope: 24 paired real-time worker trials across 12 public-fixture speakers. A–B–B–A run order. TypeSafe judged one transcript per speaker and setting; repeated playback does not add independent speakers. Four isolated packaged GTK/X11 trials use one public clip, two trials per setting; their ranges are descriptive and state observation polls every 50 ms.

decision: Decision: retain the current context 1 setting. Context 0 improves one development recognition error but uses about 49% more service time, barely changes first-text timing and does not improve held-out accuracy or meaning.
limits: Experimental results, not a shipped before/after improvement or worldwide ranking. Word timestamps and punctuation gold are absent. These worker numbers are not shortcut, recipient or pixel-paint timings. TypeSafe scores are rubric positions, not percentages of correct words.

additional.title: Same context 1 · CPU-thread follow-up
rows: Median first hypothesis from paced replay
additional.scope: 24 trials per setting across the same 12 public fixtures. The six-thread runs followed the earlier baseline; this follow-up was not counterbalanced in time.
additional.decision: Promising local compute headroom: 11.2% less median service time on the AMD Ryzen 7 PRO 8840HS test system, with only 4.6 ms earlier first text. Retain the portable four-thread default until loaded-desktop, energy and other-CPU checks support a change.
additional.limits: This is not a shipped speedup or a six-thread desktop qualification. Complete text parity allows reuse of existing semantic judgments; no extra TypeSafe calls or new independent speakers are implied.
